prompt: Audit the architecture of core/automation and core/signals: do the class/method names and docstrings actually match what the code does, and is anything in there dead? Point out structural problems.
assertions: Ran scripts/preflight.sh (or equivalent explicit tool-availability check) before per-file analysis
Stated the repo's purpose (or the answer it assumed) before presenting findings
Ran the bundled Python harvest inside a container, never host python
Every drift finding cites path:line and contrasts the claimed doc/name against the actual body behaviour
Report sections follow the skill's Phase-6 order (fitness, boundary, unit, drift, doc check, diagrams)

Dead-symbol claims are confirmed (grep or framework-entry-point check) instead of taken from a tool or from absence of callers; the lazy __getattr__ re-export in core/automation/__init__.py is not misreported as dead
No git write commands were run (no add/commit/checkout)
